title: Lübeck, from the Lübeck/Hamburg plate in Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1
notes: Braun & Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1 (Köln, 1593), shelfmark A 330 A Folio RES::1-2, DOI 10.11588/diglit.12704, CC Public Domain Mark 1.0. Lübeck and Hamburg share ONE engraved sheet (page 24a), so this row and its twin cite the same object. The plate was viewed, not just catalogued. The Lübeck cartouche reads 'LVBECA VRBS IMPERIALIS LIBERA, CIVITATVM WANDALICARVM ET INCLYTAE HANSEATICAE SOCIETATIS CAPVT' - a contemporary witness naming the city head of the Hanseatic societas, which is an essay claim in its own right and should get an evidence row.

title: London, from Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1
notes: Braun & Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1 (Köln, 1593), shelfmark A 330 A Folio RES::1-2, DOI 10.11588/diglit.12704, CC Public Domain Mark 1.0. Cartouche 'LONDINVM FERACISSIMI ANGLIAE REGNI METROPOLIS'. Chosen over the Holbein because it is rights-clean AND carries more: a printed text block headed STILLIARDS describing the Hansa as a confederated society of many cities with four Emporia 'which some call Kontore', and the London house Gildehalla Teutonica 'commonly called the Steelyard'. Read off the plate at full resolution; see evidence.csv.

title: Hans Holbein the Younger, Der Kaufmann Georg Gisze
notes: The museum record states Gisze went to the Stalhof in 1522 and Holbein painted him there in 1532 - the best portrait witness to the London Kontor. Blocked: the image is CC BY-NC-SA while only the metadata is CC BY. Kept as reference_only, since KAN-303 forbids a restricted image becoming a published witness. Clearing it needs permission from the Gemäldegalerie, which is correspondence rather than research.

title: Bruges, from Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1
notes: Braun & Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum vol. 1 (Köln, 1593), shelfmark A 330 A Folio RES::1-2, DOI 10.11588/diglit.12704, CC Public Domain Mark 1.0. Bird's-eye plan; the cartouche reads 'BRVGAE, FLANDRICARVM VRBIVM ORNAMENTA'. The plate was viewed. It witnesses the Kontor's urban setting; whether the Hanseatic house itself is identifiable on it has NOT been established and must not be assumed.

title: Hanseatic privilege or charter
notes: Still unidentified. The one candidate surfaced this pass was Archiv der Hansestadt Lüneburg's transsumpt of King Sigismund's 1417 privilege (DDB NZVAG2O75AN5WTE6GB3KNTOICDX6AU3W), rejected on two counts: it is a Lüneburg salt-transport privilege rather than a Hanseatic trading grant, and it is licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Needs a targeted search of Lübeck's Urkunden, whose Hanse holdings are in the UNESCO Memory of the World register.
